minimap_render.summary: Both defects reproduced on Xvfb :91 with the frozen binary. (a) Empty-tab bands: they appear when the last tab is closed (Ctrl+W on the only file). The editor then falls back to the special buffer `e->empty` (src/editor/buffers.c:357), which is never installed in `e->buffers[]`. The minimap worker publication path (`editor_map_receive` and `editor_map_service` in src/editor/minimap.c, both loop only over `e->buffers[]`) can never find it. The first job leaves `b->map_snapshot` set forever, so `map_due()` stays false and the map is never filled. Compose then takes the "not retained" branch in src/editor/paint.c:~295-301 and src/minimap/minimap.c:~233-262, which draws the pending scrollbar. For a 1-line buffer, every row satisfies `row_line(0) < end`, so the whole strip is a "viewport" with edge column, 3 occupied columns and wash. That gives the bright/mid/dark vertical bands. In my repro the tab strip was also blank, matching Tobias's screenshot (no tab row). A fresh Ctrl+N, a launch with no file, and a zero-byte file all render correctly (a single thin line at row 0), because those buffers are installed as tabs. (b) Fragmented stripes on big files: files over MINIMAP_SMALL_BYTES (64 KiB) or 20000 lines use `large_rows()` (src/minimap/minimap.c:~118-145). It takes at most min(256, active_rows, file_bytes/LINEIDX_CHUNK) samples, one per 64 KiB chunk, and every row in a group copies the one sample line's marks. Tobias's CONTENTS.md is 640943 bytes, so ceil(640943/65536)=10 chunks and 10 samples shared by ~1000 map rows (about 100 identical rows each). Identical marks on every row give vertical stripes. A sample landing on a blank, short or closing-tag line gives a blank gap. My 358 KB, 8000-line repro has 6 samples and shows the same pattern (a short-line band at the top, blank gaps, a stripe band). The viewport is small because it is drawn truthfully at squeeze scale: 14 px for 56 lines of 8000 (rows pixels = ~1003 for 8000 lines, ~8 lines/row). Tobias's "thin line" is the same effect, and Sublime avoids it with a fixed-scale minimap that scrolls with the document.

The map message is dropped and b->map_snapshot is never released, so map_due is false forever. Compose draws the not-retained pending scrollbar: a 1-line buffer marks every row as viewport, giving edge column, 3 occupied columns, wash and a stale bar over the full height.

root_causes: (a) e->empty (the zero-tab fallback buffer) is not registered in e->buffers[], and editor_map_receive/editor_map_service only iterate e->buffers[]; large.c:355 already special-cases e->empty for other messages, minimap.c does not. The map job's snapshot is therefore never published or released, and the pending-scrollbar fallback is what stays on screen.
(a') The pending-scrollbar fallback is not sane for lines<rows: all rows count as viewport, so it paints a full-height framed band.

(b) large_rows() samples one line per 64 KiB chunk (<=256) and broadcasts it to every row in the group; row count (~1000) greatly exceeds sample count (10 for a 640 KB file). This is an explicit design limit in minimap.h, not a rendering bug.
(b') The minimap is a squeeze-to-height design: viewport height = visible_lines * height/lines is tiny for big files, unlike Sublime's fixed-scale scrolling minimap.

find_ux.summary: Our find is a one-row, character-grid panel at the bottom of the window (src/editor/findpanel.c plus src/findui). Matching and replace are solid: all-match highlighting, N/M count, regex/case/word toggles on Alt+R/C/W, Enter and Shift+Enter, F3 and Shift+F3 with the panel closed, Ctrl+H replace, Find in Files. Almost everything that fails to feel like Sublime is ergonomics and focus. I confirmed these on Xvfb :93 with the frozen binary. (1) While the panel is open it swallows every global chord: Ctrl+W (tab stayed), Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Tab did nothing. This is the 'find then kill the tab is weird' complaint, caused by the 'consumed no-op' rule at findpanel.c:~383-391. (2) Clicking in the buffer does not move focus out of the field, so typing after a click still goes into the Find field. (3) Typing a query does not move the selection or scroll. On a 300-line file, typing 'line 250' showed count 1/1 with the view still at line 0, and only Enter jumped. Sublime selects and scrolls to the nearest match as you type. (4) Ctrl+F does not prefill from the selection; it re-selects the old query. Ctrl+E, Ctrl+Shift+E, Ctrl+F3/Ctrl+Shift+F3, Alt+F3 and Ctrl+I are all registered but marked KEYS_ARG_UNIMPLEMENTED in src/keys/keys.c. (5) Missing outright: Alt+Enter find-all (multi-select), in-selection, wrap toggle, highlight toggle, query history, Ctrl+Enter newline in the field, mouse use of the panel (the toggles are text such as '[aa]', not clickable), and a match count in the status bar (it is in the panel only). Escape closes the panel and keeps the selection, which matches Sublime. Web sources: the Sublime docs mirror https://docs.sublimetext.io/guide/usage/search-and-replace.html (shortcut tables) and https://github.com/SublimeTextIssues/Core/issues/1447 (toggle command names). The default keymap file and the official docs URLs returned 404, so panel focus semantics, incremental selection and prefill rules are recalled from experience (E), not quoted. Proposed order is focus and chord pass-through first, then incremental select, prefill and slurp, then find-all, then toggles and history.

root_causes: The find panel is modal by construction. editor_find_key (findpanel.c) runs before the global keymap for every key while find_visible is true, and consumes unknown Ctrl/Alt chords on purpose. There is no notion of 'panel open, focus in buffer'.

Panel state has one focus flag (replacement_focus) and no buffer-focus state. Only keyboard events reach the panel, and the click path in input.c has no panel hit-test, so focus cannot move by clicking.

Search is split into a worker 'preview' and an explicit navigate step. findui_next only runs from Enter or F3 (find_select_pending / find_navigated in findpanel.c), so typing never commits a selection or scroll. edit-g02 patched the symptom by making first Enter advance.

Sublime's find-adjacent commands exist as keymap rows with KEYS_ARG_UNIMPLEMENTED but have no handlers in editor_find_action (only FIND, REPLACE, FIND_NEXT/PREV, REPLACE_NEXT, TOGGLE_REGEX/CASE/WORD, FIND_IN_FILES, NEXT/PREVIOUS_RESULT).
findui_options carries only {regex, match_case, whole_word}; the search core has no in-selection or wrap parameters. Adding them touches src/findui and src/find, not only the editor glue.

modes.summary: Code-reading inventory of src/editor modal states and input routing, with no display used and nothing edited. Keyboard routing is one ordered if-ladder, editor_handle_key (input.c:1030-1068), then editor_dispatch_action (input.c:1070). Mouse and wheel go through nonkey (editor.c:571-606), then editor_pointer (input.c:1350), then editor_chrome_pointer (paint.c:389). The root cause of "find, then kill the tab" is that the find panel is a global key sink and has no separate focus state. While e->find_visible is true, editor_find_key (findpanel.c:329) consumes every key except Esc, the `common` actions and the find actions (input.c:1073-1077). A consumed Ctrl chord is a deliberate no-op (findpanel.c:352-353). That swallows Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PgUp, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+C/X, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+T, arrows and PgUp/PgDn. tests/findui_test.c:1019-1024 pins x,z,y,s,w,t as "consumed" with find open, so this is tested behaviour that has to be reversed. Menu items and palette-dispatched commands are re-fed through the same dispatcher as synthetic key events, so File > Close, Edit > Undo and Goto line are also dead while find is open. Clicking in the text does not move keyboard focus out of the panel, so typing after a click still edits the find query. Other routing problems: the palette ignores mouse clicks and middle-click paste still targets the document, and palette Ctrl/Alt chords are swallowed. Drag-and-drop does not exist: there is no plat event kind for it and no Xdnd or data_offer code on X11 or Wayland. Other risks are fatal EDITOR_ERR_INPUT_FULL when 1024 events park behind a pending open, and a fatal fail() on any nonzero rc from an input handler. Both are plausible, not reproduced.

findings.title: MODE find panel (Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H): global key sink, swallows tab/file/edit commands
findings.detail: State: e->find_visible (+ findui_panel e->find, e->find_field_all, e->find_replace_request/active, e->panel_rows via editor_text_geometry editor.c:546). There is no focus flag: while find_visible every key belongs to the panel. ROUTING (editor_handle_key -> editor_dispatch_action): (1) Esc is routed early at input.c:1046 to editor_find_key, which hides the panel (findpanel.c:338-343). (2) dispatch_action runs editor_find_action (findpanel.c:262) then, unless the binding is `common` (NEW_FILE, OPEN_FILE, SAVE_AS, EXIT, SCROLL_LINES; input.c:1073-1077), editor_find_key (findpanel.c:329). editor_find_key returns true for every other key. INTERCEPTED/handled: Esc, Enter/Shift+Enter (next/prev), Ctrl+Enter (replace one), Ctrl+Alt+Enter (replace all, replace mode), Tab (toggle fields in replace mode), Left/Right/Home/End/BackSpace/Delete and Ctrl-word variants, Ctrl+A (select field), Ctrl+V (field paste), printable text. Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and menu toggle are dispatched before the find code (input.c:1071-1072) so they do work; palette show force-hides find (palettepanel.c:8). SWALLOWED AS NO-OPS: findpanel.c:352-353 `ctrl && !enter && keysym not Left/Right/BS -> return true`, and `alt && !ctrl` (:354). So Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn, Ctrl+S, Ctrl+Z/Y, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+G, Ctrl+Shift+T, Ctrl+1..9, Alt+digit do nothing. NON-CTRL keys that are not text also vanish: Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn/F-keys fall into the final else (findpanel.c:376-396) with add=0 and are consumed (the document caret cannot be moved from the keyboard while find is open; Sublime lets arrows return focus to the buffer). Plain Tab in non-replace mode likely inserts a literal TAB into the query (ev->utf8_len path; not verified at runtime). Tested design: tests/findui_test.c:1019-1024 lists x,z,y,s,w,t as consumed with find open. HOW IT ENDS: Esc; palette show; find-in-files Enter (editor_fif_start hides it, fif.c:347); Ctrl+F again just reselects the field. It never ends on tab switch/close: editor_find_service (findpanel.c:116) silently re-targets the panel to the new active buffer, so the panel stays open across tabs. Sticky across mouse clicks: editor_pointer text clicks move the caret but find_visible stays true, so subsequent typing still goes to the query.

findings.title: MODE replace-in-progress (find_replace_active) and replace request
findings.detail: State: e->find_replace_active (+ find_replace_request 1/2 waiting for a search to finish, findpanel.c:130-135). Started by replace_begin (findpanel.c:187). ROUTING: editor_step has a dedicated branch (editor.c:825-835): while active, only queue entries that are Esc (-> editor_find_key cancels, findpanel.c:338) or PLAT_EV_CLOSE (quit) are picked; every other queued event, including tab clicks and mouse motion, stays in the queue until replace finishes. editor_activation_busy (buffers.c:347) is true so tab select/close/cycle return EDITOR_ERR_ARG if ever reached. editor_palette_show refuses (palettepanel.c:7). Ends on completion (editor_find_replace_continue -> editor_find_replace_finish input.c:1596) or Esc. RISK: events parked here accumulate toward EDITOR_INPUT_CAP=1024 (editor.h:22) and platform_event turns a full queue into fatal e->error=EDITOR_ERR_INPUT_FULL (editor.c:300); mouse MOTION events are individually queued (x11.c:666-672, no coalescing found). A long replace-all with a moving mouse is a plausible crash; needs a repro.

findings.title: MODE find in files (Ctrl+Shift+F, Where field) and Find Results tab
findings.detail: State: e->fif (editor_fif, private.h): mode, where_focus, where_all, where/where_length/where_cursor, running, done_received, results_id; panel_rows=3 when fif.mode (editor.c:546). Entered via KEYS_ACTION_FIND_IN_FILES in editor_find_action (findpanel.c:272-279): shows the find panel, fif.mode=true, cancels any running search (editor_fif_show fif.c:304). ROUTING: same find_visible sink as the plain panel, plus: Enter -> editor_fif_start (findpanel.c:359-360) which hides the panel and opens/reuses the results tab (fif.c:347+); Tab toggles where_focus (:362); with where_focus keys go to editor_fif_key (fif.c:399) and Ctrl+V to editor_fif_paste. Esc cancels a running search FIRST and leaves the panel open (input.c:1043; needs a second Esc to close panel). Results tab: derived+read_only buffer; Enter and double-click open the hit (input.c:1079-1081, 1388-1392); F4/Shift+F4 via KEYS_ACTION_NEXT/PREVIOUS_RESULT (findpanel.c:280-284); editing, cut, paste, replace refused (input.c:1144-1147, findpanel.c:188). Results assembly runs only while the results tab is the ACTIVE tab (fif.c:82-92 editor_fif_results_active, assembling): switching away pauses assembly while the job keeps running. Closing the results tab does not cancel the job (no fif reference in buffers.c close path); editor_fif_pending stays true until the worker's DONE arrives. Ends: search DONE, Esc, new search (old job retires), editor_fif_close at exit.

findings.title: MODE command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P)
findings.detail: State: e->palette_open, palette_owner/generation/revision, palette_state e->palette. Opened by editor_palette_show (palettepanel.c:5), dispatched BEFORE find handling (input.c:1071). ROUTING: editor_handle_key checks palette_open right after the close prompt (input.c:1034), before menu, stale prompt and find. editor_palette_key (palettepanel.c:30): Esc closes; Enter runs the selected row by synthesising a key event and calling editor_dispatch_action (:42-46); Up/Down move; BackSpace and text edit the query. Any Ctrl/Super or non-AltGr Alt chord is swallowed (`return 0`, :35-36), so Ctrl+Shift+P cannot toggle it closed, Ctrl+W/Tab do nothing; Left/Right/Home/End/PgUp/PgDn/Delete are ignored. Mouse: nonkey has no palette_open check, so a click in the text moves the caret behind the palette, middle-click pastes PRIMARY into the document (editor.c:576-577), wheel scrolls; palette rows are not clickable. Ends: Esc, Enter, focus loss (editor.c:586-587 editor_palette_close), and editor_palette_sync closes it when the owner buffer id, source generation or REVISION changes (palettepanel.c:23-28) - a tab click, a file change on disk or an IPC open closes it. Opening it hides find (palettepanel.c:8).

findings.title: MODE menu bar (Alt tap, Alt+mnemonic, click) incl. pinned/active/open
findings.detail: State: e->menu {pinned, config_visible, armed, was_active, active, open, title, item, first}. Visible = pinned||active||open>=0 and costs one row (editor_text_geometry editor.c:539). KEYS: editor_menu_key (menubar.c:90) is called from editor_handle_key (input.c:1038-1042) only when no go-to prompt and no stale source, and AFTER the palette check, so Alt does nothing while the palette is open. A bare Alt press+release arms then latches focus; Alt+letter opens a menu unless that chord is bound (:122-131); while latched, Esc/arrows/Enter/mnemonics are handled and every other key is swallowed (:150-153); a Ctrl/Super chord closes the menu then falls through and runs (:138-141). MOUSE: editor_menu_pointer (menubar.c:183) is called first in nonkey (editor.c:600) unless the buffer is stale: title click opens/closes, an item click runs, any other click while latched closes the bar; a pinned idle bar leaves other clicks alone. Items run via editor_dispatch_action with a synthetic event (menubar.c:66-72), so they inherit the find-panel sink (File > Close, Edit > Undo, Goto line do nothing while find is open) and the go-to prompt's lookup suppression. Ends: Esc, Enter/run, outside click, focus loss (editor_menu_reset editor.c:587). Also affects the close prompt: editor_close_prompt_shown requires menu.open<0 && !menu.active (buffers.c:610-613), so opening the menu silently cancels a pending close prompt.

findings.title: MODE go-to-line / Open file / Save As prompt (e->go)
findings.detail: State: editor_go go {active, kind (GOTO_LINE/OPEN_FILE/SAVE_AS), digits[], length, cursor, selected, valid, accept, owner, generation, original view + scroll}. Entered via goto_key when the action is GOTO_LINE, OPEN_FILE or SAVE_AS (input.c:1129-1130, 1177; goto_key 863). It draws on the last grid row (editor_goto_overlay paint.c:462). ROUTING: when go.active the keymap lookup is skipped entirely (input.c:1065 `result = e->go.active ? KEYS_NONE`), find and fif code is skipped (`!e->go.active`, input.c:1076,1079), and ALL keys go to goto_key: Esc cancels (restores original viewport), Enter commits (goto: seek and accept; open/save-as: sets e->file_command and queues work), Ctrl+A selects, arrows/Home/End/BackSpace/Delete edit, text inserts (digits only for goto). Any other Ctrl/Alt chord is ignored by falling to `editor_full_layout` (input.c:924). So Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+F are dead inside the prompt - consistent, but nothing tells the user. MOUSE: nonkey cancels the prompt on a button PRESS (restoring the viewport) and then the click proceeds; motion/release are dropped while active (editor.c:601-602). A tab click therefore cancels and switches. Go-to line also previews as you type (scroll jumps while typing, restored on Esc). Ends: Enter, Esc, mouse press, owner buffer id/generation change or stale source (input.c:1049-1053), editor_goto_cancel input.c:803. Note editor_open path: Open file is a typed-path prompt (no file dialog).

findings.title: MODE close-modified-tab prompt (status row: S save / D don't save / Esc cancel)
findings.detail: State: e->close_prompt {owner, prompt_ns, prompt_serial, saving}. Created by editor_close_request (buffers.c:596) from Ctrl+W/CLOSE_FILE (input.c:1206) for a modified, non-derived, non-placeholder tab. ROUTING: close_prompt_key is the FIRST check in editor_handle_key (input.c:1033). Keys typed before the prompt frame was submitted are swallowed (prompt_ns/prompt_serial gate); repeats and Ctrl/Alt/Super chords are swallowed; S saves (Save As prompt for untitled, then the tab closes in maintenance editor_close_service buffers.c:625 once the save leaves it unmodified), D discards, Esc cancels. All other keys are SWALLOWED while shown (returns true), so Ctrl+Tab/typing are dead. MOUSE: not gated. Clicking a tab calls editor_activate which clears owner when the buffer changes (buffers.c:358); clicks in text and wheel work with the prompt still shown; middle-click paste still edits the buffer. The prompt is cancelled silently when go.active, palette_open or the menu is active (editor_close_prompt_shown buffers.c:608-613, checked at input.c:1009, paint.c:529). It does NOT account for find_visible: Ctrl+W never gets here while find is open (see find finding), and if both are visible the overlay overwrites the last row (find panel's final row), hiding the field. A failed/cancelled save leaves the tab open with no message beyond save_error. Close refused (all closed-tab slots modified) shows a notice (buffers.c:586-590).

findings.title: MODE source-changed prompt (R reload / K keep) and pending_open / placeholder
findings.detail: State: editor_buffer.source_stale + prompt_ns/prompt_serial/prompt_generation; e->source_choice (editor_check_sources buffers.c:1129). Set when the file changes on disk and the buffer has unsaved edits (clean buffers reload silently, buffers.c:1138). ROUTING: in editor_handle_key after the find Esc code (input.c:1056-1063): while source_stale and the key is not in editor_event_control (input.c:958-985: next/prev view, close, close_file, reopen, select tab, font size, exit, save, new file, open file), only plain r/R (reload) and k/K (keep) act, after the prompt frame was submitted; everything else (typing, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+G, Save As, Ctrl+Shift+P, menu Alt - input.c:1038 skips the menu when stale) is dropped with no feedback. Control keys then still pass through editor_dispatch_action, where an open find panel swallows them. MOUSE: editor_menu_pointer skipped; editor_pointer routes only tab-strip clicks (editor_event_control for MOUSE = y within the tab rows, input.c:962-965); text clicks, wheel (editor_handle_wheel:1306) and minimap drag are disabled. Ends on R/K (applied in maintenance, may be deferred while a save is active), or Reload/Keep rewrites source_stale=false. pending_open (async large-file open): same event_control passthrough, all other events are PARKED in the queue with queue_owner (editor.c:656-671, editor_inject:676-679) - motion events included, so the 1024-event cap (editor.h:22 -> fatal EDITOR_ERR_INPUT_FULL, editor.c:300) is reachable during a long open while the mouse moves (needs repro).

findings.title: MODE minimap drag (e->map_drag) and tab drag-reorder (e->drag_tab/drag_id)
findings.detail: State: map_drag/map_drag_id/map_drag_generation/map_drag_offset; drag_tab/drag_id. Both live in editor_chrome_pointer (paint.c:389-457), reached from editor_pointer when the event is not a text press/drag (input.c:1357-1367). Press on the minimap column (col >= text cols, row >= tab_rows) sets map_drag and map_grab (paint.c:343) decides whether the press lands in the painted viewport band (keeps the grab offset) or recenters the band on the click; motion while map_drag seeks via minimap_hit/minimap_hit_approx and editor_scroll_seek; release (BUTTON code 1 !press) clears both drags (paint.c:394). Cleared also on tab activate, resize, focus change (editor.c:582,592, buffers.c:339-341) and when the buffer goes stale/pending. Interaction holes: (a) editor_pointer clears text_drag first but nothing clears map_drag when the release arrives while go.active (nonkey drops releases at editor.c:601-602); go.active during a drag requires a key chord mid-drag, rare. (b) map_drag does not consult palette/find/close-prompt state: dragging works behind a palette or close prompt. (c) map_grab / minimap_hit use e->map_grid.dims.cell_h pixels and sampled/approx summaries for large files; the 'indicator does not follow the cursor on big files' complaint belongs here (the retained vs unretained band at paint.c:352-367 and the approx seek at 430-440), analysed by the minimap agent.

findings.title: MODE text drag-select, multi-click chain, edge autoscroll
findings.detail: State: e->text_drag, text_drag_id/generation, text_drag_mode (1 shift-extend, 2 word, 3 line/gutter), click_ns/row/col/count/button/id/generation, text_pointer, text_drag_pixels, text_drag_rehit, pointer_unit_pending. editor_pointer (input.c:1350): left press in the text rect starts it; motion with text_drag extends; release clears (input.c:1352). Edge distance beyond the text rect autoscrolls from editor_pointer_tick (input.c:1452) once per completed frame. Cancels: tab switch (buffers.c:339-341), resize/focus (editor.c:582,592), source generation change (input.c:1359-1360), palette show (palettepanel.c:11). It is NOT cancelled by opening find or the menu, and the pointer path has no palette/find/prompt awareness: a click while the palette or close prompt is shown moves the document caret and starts a selection behind it. Double-click on a Find Results line opens the hit (input.c:1388-1392). Wrapped and unwrapped hit-testing differ (scroll_frame_hit only when !wrap && !panel_rows, input.c:1380): while the find panel is open (panel_rows>0) clicks use the non-plan row mapping.

findings.title: MODE scroll / wheel / byte-seek (wheel_pending, find_scroll, scroll_pending, queued pages)
findings.detail: State: e->wheel_pending, find_scroll, wheel (scroll_state), wrap_wheel_rows; per buffer scroll_pending, scroll_following, scroll_queued_pages/wheel/pixels, scroll_resident. Wheel: PLAT_EV_WHEEL -> editor_handle_wheel (input.c:1304) - ignored when stale/pending_open/no tab; NOT gated by palette/find/menu/prompt/go (wheel works under every overlay and under go-to preview). During an unresolved byte jump (find result far away, minimap seek) wheel and PgUp/PgDn are queued for the landed top (edit-pd6, input.c:1313-1316, 1228-1233). Any click or minimap press clears wheel_pending/find_scroll (input.c:1394, paint.c:420). Ctrl+Up/Down (SCROLL_LINES) is `common` so it works with find open (input.c:1073-1075). Home/End/Ctrl+End supersede a pending jump. editor_wheel_continue/editor_scroll_slice advance it from editor_step (editor.c:793).

findings.title: MODE pending file command (Ctrl+N / Ctrl+O / Save As confirm) and in-flight save, Save As, checkpoint publish
findings.detail: State: e->file_command (+path/owner/generation); editor_save_leased(e) (session.c:538: e->publish or save journal_leased), editor_save_active (session.c:547: saving, publish, save_as), e->save_as, publish_owed. Ctrl+N sets file_command at input.c:1103-1108; Ctrl+O/Save As use the e->go prompt then Enter sets file_command (input.c:878-886). queue_pick returns SIZE_MAX (consumes no input at all) while file_command is set or the journal is leased (editor.c:655-656): ALL input incl. clicks and mouse motion is parked, only PLAT_EV_CLOSE bypasses (editor_inject:675). editor_file_command_service (commands.c:274) runs in maintenance once not dirty/active; if the active buffer changed meanwhile it silently drops the command (commands.c:280). Open failure shows 'open failed' notice only. Save (Ctrl+S): editor_save_request (input.c:1116) is a no-op on derived/placeholder; save success/failure appears on the status row (session.c save status ~:745), with S-from-close-prompt chaining. Parked events count toward the 1024-event fatal cap (see above). Ctrl+S is swallowed by an open find panel.

findings.title: MODE clipboard in flight (EDITOR_ACTION_CLIP, middle-click paste)
findings.detail: State: e->action==EDITOR_ACTION_CLIP, editor_clip (c->waiting, hitting, primary_waiting). Ctrl+C/X/V go through editor_clip_action (input.c:1139-1148) AFTER find handling, so with find open copy/cut/paste in the document are dead (Ctrl+V pastes into the find field instead via editor_clip_find_paste). Middle-click (button 2) and PLAT_EV_CLIPBOARD are routed straight to editor_clip_event in nonkey (editor.c:576-577) before every overlay check: with the palette, menu, go-to or close prompt open, middle-click still pastes PRIMARY into the document (clip.c:476-483 guards only stale/pending_open/busy). While editor_clip_busy, queue_pick lets only CLIPBOARD events through (editor.c:657-661); no timeout is visible in clip.c for a selection owner that never replies (platform-level failure event code 1 clears waiting, clip.c:489) - unverified for a hung owner.

findings.title: MODE tab cycling (Ctrl+Tab MRU) and tab-strip mouse
findings.detail: State: tabs.cycling (MRU walk), released on Ctrl key-up in editor_handle_key (input.c:1065-1067), focus loss/keymap events (editor.c:597). Ctrl+Tab/Ctrl+Shift+Tab (NEXT/PREVIOUS_VIEW_STACK) -> editor_cycle_tab; Ctrl+PgDn/PgUp -> adjacent; Alt+1..9 select. All gated by editor_activation_busy, which returns EDITOR_ERR_ARG (a hard error, because editor_step turns any non-zero input rc into fatal fail(), editor.c:862-863, 117-122) when view_busy, a clip, a save lease, replace-all or EDITOR_ACTION_GOTO is active; queue_pick/step ordering currently keeps those states from dispatching tab commands, but that invariant is the whole safety net and is worth a matrix test. Tab strip mouse: editor_chrome_pointer (paint.c:396-403): press selects and starts a drag-reorder; no close button and no middle-click-close exist in tabs_strip_hit (tabs.h:120) - middle-click on the strip goes to clipboard code. Find panel/palette state is not reset on a tab click except the palette (revision/owner sync); the find panel survives and retargets (findpanel.c:116-139).

findings.title: GLOBAL ACTIONS matrix inputs: how each reaches (or fails to reach) its handler with each mode open
findings.detail: Order of checks in editor_handle_key (input.c:1030): 1 close_prompt_key; 2 palette (editor_palette_key); 3 menu keys (skipped if stale or go.active); 4 Esc cancels running find-in-files; 5 Esc closes find; 6 go-to staleness cleanup; 7 stale-source filter (R/K only, except editor_event_control keys); 8 key release handling (Ctrl-up releases MRU); 9 config_keys_lookup (skipped while go.active); 10 editor_dispatch_action: palette-open and menu toggle first, then `common` bypass list, then editor_find_action/editor_find_key (find sink), then fif Enter, modifier-only keys dropped, then EXIT, NEW_FILE, CANCEL, SAVE, FONT_SIZE, clip, tab group, undo/redo, edit/move/text. Per global action: Close tab Ctrl+W: dead in find/palette/go/stale-find; prompts for modified tabs (close prompt), immediate for derived/results tabs. New tab Ctrl+N and Open Ctrl+O, Save As, Exit, Ctrl+Up/Down: common, work with find open (o20). Ctrl+Tab / Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn / Alt+N: dead in find, palette, go, close prompt; pass in stale. Save Ctrl+S: dead in find; passes in stale; no-op on derived. Undo/Redo: dead in find (swallowed), palette, go. Ctrl+F again: reselects the field (field_select_all) and resets mode; closed by go-to, close prompt, palette, stale (stale swallows it since not event-control). Palette: opens over everything except go.active and stale and replace-all; closes find; close prompt cancelled. Menu Alt: blocked by palette, go, stale; cancels close prompt. Click in text: moves caret in every state except stale/pending_open (silently ignored); cancels go; does not move key focus out of find; does nothing to palette. Click on tab: cancels go, closes palette via sync, clears close prompt if tab differs, keeps find open. dnd.summary: Confirmed: drop is not implemented on X11, Win32 or in the editor. A grep for Xdnd, XdndAware, WM_DROPFILES, IDropTarget and DragAcceptFiles across src finds nothing. The X11 window's event mask and properties (src/x11/x11.c:525-547) have no XdndAware, and XCB_CLIENT_MESSAGE handles only WM_DELETE_WINDOW (x11.c:642). Wayland binds wl_data_device only for the clipboard (wayland.c:424-468); device_enter/drop even say "file drops outside this backend's scope" and do nothing (wayland.c:388-402). The cheapest route on X11 is to reuse the existing selection receive machinery in src/x11/clip.c (INCR, timeouts, budgets, tested against a raw-xcb peer in tests/x11_clip_test.c) with XdndSelection as a third selection and text/uri-list as the target. Add a small platform-neutral hand-off, e.g. a PLAT_EV_DROP event plus plat_drop_data() mirroring plat_clip_data(), then a pure URI-list parser that fills an ipc_request and calls editor_open_request() on the UI thread. That is exactly what CLI and second-instance opens already do (src/editor/buffers.c:807), and it already handles de-duplication, tab selection and activation. Limits to respect: IPC_MAX_PATHS=128 and IPC_PATH_CAP=4096 (src/ipc/ipc.h:9-10), and ipc_path.path is a borrowed const char* so the parser needs a UI-owned scratch arena. The drop payload is small, so reading it on the UI thread via the async clip state machine does not break the no-blocking rule; Wayland reads from a nonblocking pipe pumped by the loop, as the clipboard already does. Folder-to-sidebar (Sublime behaviour) cannot be done because no sidebar UI exists yet (only sidebar_revision fields in editor.h:38), so v1 should open files only and ignore or report directories. Beads: 1) pure parser, 2) X11 XDND target, 3) editor wiring plus UX, 4) Wayland, 5) Win32. I did not run the editor under Xvfb. Nemo's offered target types are unverified from here (E), so bead 2 includes a one-off logger step.

findings.detail: No XdndAware property is set, no Xdnd client messages are handled. Wayland device_enter calls wl_data_offer_accept(offer, serial, NULL) (a NULL mime means reject) and drop just destroys the offer. The manager is bound at version 1, so set_actions/finish (v3) are unavailable. Win32 has no WM_DROPFILES/DragAcceptFiles. plat_event has no path or payload field.

Window creation sets the event mask, WM_PROTOCOLS, _NET_WM_NAME and PID, then stops; no extra mask bit is needed because ClientMessage is delivered regardless.

findings.detail: clip.c already implements async ConvertSelection plus property read, INCR, timeouts and memory budget. XdndSelection is an ordinary selection owned by the source window, so a receive for target text/uri-list, selection XdndSelection, timestamp from XdndDrop data.l[2], is the same flow. SELECTION_NOTIFY is routed via x11_clip_event (x11.c:674). Needs: a third selection id and a target atom parameter. The clip request is currently UTF8/text-plain only, so it must be generalised or a parallel small receiver added.

Two other callers already do this on the UI thread (IPC drain buffers.c:906, find-in-files fif.c:489).

The Wayland and X11 backends both implement the accessor; Win32 can queue the converted UTF-8 list the same way.

root_causes: The X11 window never sets the XdndAware property, so XDND sources do not target it (no XdndEnter ever arrives).
The X11 ClientMessage handler only recognises WM_DELETE_WINDOW; none of the Xdnd messages are handled, and nothing replies with XdndStatus/XdndFinished.
Wayland accepts the drag offer with a NULL mime type, a rejection, and discards it on drop; the data-device manager is bound at version 1 so there is no set_actions/finish.
The platform event model (plat_event, plat.h) has no drop event or payload accessor, and no URI-list parser exists.
Win32 layer does not call DragAcceptFiles and has no WM_DROPFILES case.

proposed_beads.title: Drop: pure text/uri-list and file URI parser
proposed_beads.scope: New module src/dnd (dnd.h, dnd.c): parse a text/uri-list byte buffer (RFC 2483: CRLF or LF separated lines, '#' comment lines skipped, blank lines skipped, no NUL) into at most IPC_MAX_PATHS UTF-8 paths in a caller-provided arena, filling ipc_request. Accept file:///p, file://localhost/p, file://<this-host>/p (compare against gethostname); reject other hosts; reject non-file schemes; percent-decode (%XX, UTF-8 passthrough, reject %00 and bad hex); skip entries over IPC_PATH_CAP; report skipped count. Also a bare absolute path line (some sources send plain paths). Skip directories only at open time, not here. No malloc: arena only. Pure, no X dependency, so Win32 and Wayland reuse it.

tstack.summary: Found it: github.com/t3dotgg/tstack (Theo Browne), "agent skills I use every day", 9 skills, latest commit 2026-10-27. The council skill is `skills/council/SKILL.md`, triggered by the word "council". It is a code/PR-review loop, NOT a design hill-climb: the README lists no design skill, and the skill contains no rubric, screenshot judging or design criteria. Mechanism (read verbatim via gh api): the orchestrator spawns three read-only delegates in parallel, one flagship model per provider at high reasoning effort (default example Claude Opus, GPT Sol, Gemini Pro; user may name members; if a provider is unreachable it reports rather than substitutes). Each gets the request plus context. For code review each returns a score out of 10; one full pass is a round and a fresh review after fixes starts a new round. The orchestrator summarizes findings/disagreements, makes the changes it agrees with, requests a fresh review, and repeats until all delegates are satisfied. Disagreement is resolved by the orchestrating agent's judgment (no vote rule), and it is told to fight scope creep. Results go in a "Council review" table (rounds x delegate scores, "no score" if absent) in the PR description. The stopping rule is only "all delegates satisfied"; no numeric threshold or round cap in council itself. The sibling skill sol-loop adds a budget (3 rounds, extend to 5 for security/data-loss, stop on nit-only round, single reviewer, findings ledger). Tobias has nothing named tstack locally (find and ~/.claude/skills checked). Tobias's design hill-climb would be an adaptation: council's loop shape plus a design rubric and rendered screenshots that tstack does not supply. Tobias lacks Gemini (he said so), so the council would be Opus plus Sol (two providers), which council's rule would report as unavailable unless he names members explicitly.

best_design.summary: Awards are a poor guide for grading a code editor. The 2026 Apple Design Award winners (12 of them, announced 2 June 2026) are consumer apps and games (grug, Moonlitt, Tide Guide, Guitar Wiz, Cyberpunk 2077 and others), and the 2025 winners are the same kind (CapWords, Taobao, Speechify, Watch Duty, Feather). Red Dot Brands & Communication Design 2026 winners are not public until 6 Nov 2026, and I found no iF 2026 software winners. So the useful exemplars are working tools: Linear, Zed, Sublime, Ghostty, iA Writer, Things, Nova, Raycast, plus the type and colour systems behind them (Geist, JetBrains Mono, Commit Mono, Radix). docs/design/state-of-design-2026.md and the 2026-10-21 workups already settled palette, motion and type choices, so this adds only what they lack: the exact defaults of the editors Tobias compares against (Zed, VS Code, Sublime), which are the nearest evidence for minimap and find-panel design. Three transferable decisions came out of that. First, Zed ships the minimap off, with a left-open thumb border and a width capped at 80 columns. VS Code's is proportional, shows characters, and reveals its slider on mouseover. Sublime's minimap scrolls with the document on huge files and its click-to-scroll is known to miss there (forum). Second, Linear's 2026 refresh gives the clearest rules for chrome: dim what is not the work, fewer and softer dividers, compact non-full-width tabs, "structure should be felt, not seen". Third, the right-hand column is where eyes go, and sublimité's minimap thumb is the loudest thing there. The deliverable ends with 10 criteria scored 1 to 5 for a council of Sol and Opus, and with beads that build the grading harness before any design change. Caveats: Raycast 2.0 details come from third-party summaries; the Linear, Zed, Ghostty and VS Code numbers are from primary sources; designer attributions for Inter, JetBrains Mono, Monaspace and iA Writer come from my training knowledge and were not re-fetched.

findings.title: Exemplar: Linear (desktop app, March 2026 refresh)
findings.detail: Observable decisions: sidebar made 'a few notches dimmer' than the work area; tab bar made compact, not full-width, with rounded corners and smaller icon and text; coloured team-icon backgrounds removed; dividers fewer and lower contrast ('structure should be felt, not seen'); palette moved from cool blue-ish grey to a warmer, less saturated grey ('too warm risks looking muddy'); success test 'if most people don't immediately notice what changed, that's a good sign'. Process: a dev toolbar toggles old vs new in one click (so a council can A/B), and a colour tool exposes hue/chroma/lightness per token (earlier theme system used 3 inputs: base, accent, contrast). Transfers: tab shape, divider policy, dim-the-periphery rule, the A/B toggle as a grading mechanism. Does not transfer: icon-heavy sidebar, rounded pills at cell-grid cost.

findings.title: Exemplar: Zed (editor defaults as a design statement)
findings.detail: Defaults from assets/settings/default.json: minimap show 'never', thumb 'always', thumb_border 'left_open', max_width_columns 80; tabs close button 'hover', diagnostics off, git status off; search_on_type true, seed_search_query_from_cursor 'always', search_wrap true; scrollbar auto-hides and carries search results, selected text/symbol, diagnostics and git marks as ticks (the scrollbar does the minimap's job); cursor bar, blink on; buffer 15 / UI 16, line height 'comfortable' (1.618 per prior doc); status bar shows cursor position and language only, line endings and non-UTF-8 encoding only when unusual. Theme Builder (Feb 2026) links tokens (focus border, icon-to-text, shared panel/tab/surface base) so a theme cannot drift; 16 UI colour categories, 10 syntax. 1.9.0 (June 2026) added a project-search picker with live preview and resizable picker modals. Transfers: off-by-default minimap plus information-bearing scrollbar; incremental find seeded from the cursor; status bar that shows only what is non-default.

findings.title: Exemplar: VS Code (the minimap and find reference)
findings.detail: Minimap defaults from editorOptions.ts: enabled true, size 'proportional', side right, showSlider 'mouseover', renderCharacters true, maxColumn 120, scale 1, autohide none. Scrollbar 14 px vertical, 12 px horizontal. Find: seedSearchStringFromSelection 'always', addExtraSpaceOnTop true (the page scrolls so the first line is not hidden under the find widget), loop true, globalFindClipboard false. Caret smoothing and smooth scrolling off. Transfers: slider only on hover; find widget must not occlude text (addExtraSpaceOnTop is the exact fix for 'find covers my code'); 'proportional' means the map shrinks to the file only up to a cap, so a huge file gives a viewport slider of a few pixels, which is the 'thin line' Tobias saw and which Sublime avoids by scrolling the map.

findings.title: Exemplar: Sublime Text 4 (the reference Tobias grades against)
findings.detail: Build 4213 (21 Sep 2026) is current; GPU rendering since 4.0. Minimap: viewport box hidden until hover by default; forum reports that on files too tall for the map, the map itself scrolls with the document and click-to-scroll then misses (developer: it cannot satisfy all expectations); `minimap_scroll_to_clicked_text` false is a workaround that felt jittery. The settings page does not document defaults (they are in Preferences > Settings), so I could not extract minimap_style or find-panel defaults; they need a look at the real app. Transfers: the large-file minimap model (scrolling map plus viewport that tracks the document) is the behaviour Tobias asked for, and its known weakness (click mapping while the map scrolls) is a design constraint to test.

findings.title: Exemplar: Ghostty and Zed rendering (already in prior doc, here only the delta)
findings.detail: Ghostty: native widgets, cursor styles block/bar/underline/block_hollow, blink on unless the app requests otherwise, unfocused splits dimmed (minimum opacity 0.15 per config reference). Prior doc already has linear-corrected blending and Zed gamma 1.8. Transfer not yet in the workups: dimming of the unfocused pane/window as the focus signal instead of borders, which fits an editor with several windows or a find bar that holds focus.

findings.title: Exemplar: iA Writer and Things (restraint and focus)
findings.detail: iA Writer: deliberately few features; monospace chosen 'because we want people to slow down' (founder quote via Macworld); Focus Mode dims everything except the current sentence/paragraph; the Mono/Duo/Quattro family modified from IBM Plex to remove IBM-typical round dots. Things (Apple Design Award 2009 and 2017): 'never feels messy or overbearing no matter the length of the list', animations keep your place, top-rated keyboard support. Transfer: focus dimming as an optional mode; emptiness as a feature; animation only to preserve spatial continuity (never on the typing path, per Law 2 and prior doc section 5). Evidence for Things is reviewer praise, not a design post.

findings.title: Exemplar: Nova (Panic) and Raycast (weak evidence, flagged)
findings.detail: Nova: MacStories credits 'Mac-like' care: a real preferences pane instead of JSON, functional sidebar, git status in sidebar and editor; one developer-forum thread notes horizontal tabs crowd with many files. Raycast: stated principles fast, simple, delightful (official blog); 'Cmd-N picks the Nth result' with shortcuts shown inline (third-party analysis); 2.0 left beta 25 Aug 2026 and restyled for Liquid Glass (third-party, unverified); a motion token file listing 150/200 ms is a derived 'inspired by' file and must not be cited as Raycast's own. Transfer: discoverable shortcuts shown inline in palette rows; palette as a list with numbered picks. Do not transfer glass.

findings.title: Type and colour systems worth borrowing from
findings.detail: Geist (Vercel with Basement Studio and Andres Briganti; influences Inter, Univers, SF Mono, Suisse, Diatype; Geist Mono meant for editors and terminals, OFL). Commit Mono (Eigil Nikolajsen; cites Jasper Morrison's Super Normal manifesto; weight 400 recommended for dark and 450 for light, so weight should follow theme; ligatures off by default; OFL). JetBrains Mono (Philipp Nurullin and Konstantin Bulenkov, from training knowledge). Inter (Rasmus Andersson), Monaspace (GitHub Next with Lettermatic), iA fonts (Oliver Reichenstein) are from training knowledge. Radix 12-step scale: 1-2 app/subtle background, 3-5 component fill rest/hover/active, 6-8 borders (subtle, interactive, strong/focus), 9-10 solid, 11 low-contrast text, 12 high-contrast text; for dark mode use step 1 or 2 as app background. New fact for sublimite: Commit Mono's advice that dark mode wants a lighter weight than light mode is a gradeable decision (does text weight differ between themes?).

findings.title: Rubric for the council: 10 criteria, each scored 1 to 5 on a screenshot
findings.detail:
Scale for every criterion: 1 = the failure named; 3 = acceptable default; 5 = exemplar-level. Contrast numbers are WCAG 2.2 ratios, computed as in docs/design/workups-2026-10-21/README.md (P).
C1 Type size and rendering. 1: glyphs under 3 mm on the glass, or blurry/uneven stem weight, or a missing-glyph box. 3: legible, em about 28 px at 192-243 DPI (prior doc: 30 px = 3.14 mm), even weight. 5: crisp even stems, no fringes, one face with a fallback chain, line pitch a whole number of pixels, weight chosen per theme.
C2 Contrast hierarchy. 1: UI chrome or minimap brighter than code text. 3: text at least 4.5:1, chrome below text. 5: strict ladder text > muted > gutter > minimap > hairline, comments readable at 4.5:1 or more, nothing but the caret and current match saturated.
C3 Colour discipline. 1: more than one accent, pure red/green/yellow, pure #FFF on #000. 3: one accent, syntax hues clearly distinct. 5: one accent used only for caret, focus and current match; five or fewer low-chroma syntax hues at similar lightness; neutral greys share one tint; light and dark both pass.
C4 Chrome density and quietness. 1: chrome competes with text (heavy borders, bright tab strip, labels touching edges). 3: chrome is flat and dimmer than the page. 5: Linear test, the active tab joins the page, structure felt not seen, at most hairline dividers, nothing in chrome that does no work.
C5 Tab bar. 1: separators or markers as characters (| or *), no clear active tab. 3: clear active tab, readable labels. 5: compact, active tab continuous with the page, unsaved shown by a dot, close button on hover, overflow has a defined behaviour.
C6 Status and gutter. 1: status line shouts or is missing information needed to work; gutter numbers as bright as code. 3: dim numbers, status with position. 5: current line number brighter than others, status shows only what is useful and non-default, readable in one glance, same grey family as chrome.
C7 Minimap and scrollbar. 1: the map is the loudest column, or a huge file shows a hairline viewport, or the viewport does not track the pointer. 3: quiet texture, visible viewport. 5: map quieter than text, viewport visible and draggable at the pointer on a 1 GiB file (map scrolls like Sublime or has a defined minimum viewport height), scroll marks for find matches and caret.
C8 Find and palette panel. 1: panel hides the match or changes layout under the user, Escape or tab close is ambiguous. 3: incremental find with a visible count. 5: search-as-you-type seeded from the selection, match count and current match emphasised, text never occluded (VS Code addExtraSpaceOnTop), one key to dismiss and focus returns to the caret, palette rows show shortcuts inline.
C9 Selection, caret and match states. 1: states indistinguishable (selection vs find vs current line). 3: all four distinct. 5: selection about 24-27 percent accent over the page, current match different from other matches, 2 px bar caret that stays solid while typing, active line fill barely visible.
C10 Empty and edge states. 1: broken layout in an empty tab, giant gaps, stale overlays. 3: blank page with intact chrome. 5: calm single-line empty state, minimap absent or consistent, no artefacts after any sequence of open/close/find.
Each criterion can be graded from a still image except motion; motion (no animation on keyboard actions, one frame maximum) is graded from the code or a frame-timing note, not from screenshots, so it is left out of the ten.
findings.evidence: Built from sources above plus docs/design/state-of-design-2026.md sections 3, 4, 7 and workups README table (derivations there)

root_causes: The design has no gradeable standard: edit-b0j (visual spec, P0) is still open since 2026-10-10, and the five workups exist as pictures but nothing scores shipped screenshots against them.

Awards (Apple Design Awards, Red Dot, iF) reward consumer apps and games; no code editor appears, so they cannot be the council's reference. The credible reference set is Linear, Zed, Sublime, VS Code, Ghostty, iA Writer.

The minimap complaints (empty tab artefacts, hairline viewport on big files) are a design-spec gap as well as bugs: Zed ships the minimap off, VS Code caps and shows the slider on hover, and Sublime scrolls the map on huge files; sublimite has no stated rule for any of these cases.

council.summary: Protocol: a deterministic scene-capture harness (private Xvfb, frozen fixtures, 6 scenes x 2 themes = 12 PNGs, P: 6x2) feeds a two-member council (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh and Claude Opus; no Gemini) that scores each scene 1-5 on 10 rubric criteria with written evidence. Grading is blind and pairwise (candidate vs current baseline, random A/B order, no mention of which is new), plus one sighted pass after to name fixes. The council only ranks and proposes; a change lands only if the council median rises with no regressed criterion AND Tobias's eye approves a before/after sheet (Law 1: use is the gate, scores are advisory). Loop shape is borrowed from tstack council (parallel read-only delegates, scores per round, orchestrator judges disagreements, scope-creep guard) with sol-loop's stopping rules; tstack has no design content, so the rubric, screenshots and A/B logic are ours. Awards (Apple Design Awards, Red Dot, iF) are consumer-app oriented, so the references are working tools: Sublime (baseline Tobias grades against), Zed, Linear, VS Code, Ghostty, iA Writer; Tobias should confirm the list. Reference images come only from public marketing pages/press kits/docs (used for private grading, never redistributed or committed) or Tobias's own captures; Sublime and Zed can be captured by Tobias on his machine. Codex accepts images (`codex exec -i/--image`, verified in --help), so both members see PNGs directly. Cost per iteration is 4 sighted-batch calls per candidate-vs-baseline blind pass (2 members x 2 themes, P: 2x2), plus 2 for the sighted fix pass; per-scene calls (24, P: 2x12) are the fallback if a batch hides detail. The first thing to build is the capture script, then the scoring runner; neither changes the editor. Design changes themselves reuse the existing workups (01 Quiet tokens is S and 0 B memory per its README) as the first candidate, which also exercises the loop end to end.

findings.title: Scenes: fixed matrix, rendered deterministically
findings.detail: Scenes (6): S1 empty tab; S2 C source file (a frozen copy of src/piece/piece.c lines, same as workups baseline); S3 find open with matches and a current match; S4 palette open; S5 many tabs (enough to overflow the strip; count chosen as strip width / min label width, derived at build time, not guessed); S6 large file with minimap (generated by tools/mkcorpus to a fixed size and seed, scrolled to a fixed offset). x 2 themes (dark, light) = 12 PNGs (P: 6x2). Determinism: private Xvfb at 3296x2060x24, -dpi 192 (as given in the topic brief; workups used 243 DPI, so pin one and record it in the manifest), -noreset, private XDG dirs, EDIT_REFUSE_REAL_DISPLAY=1 (src/main.c:34), reuse tools/with_display_lock.sh for the display guard, fixed window size via xdotool, fixed fonts (fonts-go + Noto Emoji per memory note), caret blink frozen or sampled at a fixed phase, mouse parked off-window, wait for N identical consecutive captures before saving (stability check), and run twice and byte-compare as the self-test; differing regions are reported, not hidden.
findings.evidence: src/main.c:34; Makefile:193 SAFE_DISPLAY; tools/with_display_lock.sh:37; docs/design/workups-2026-10-21/README.md (baseline.png on private Xvfb :96)

findings.title: References: legal sourcing
findings.detail: Exemplar images are inputs to private grading only; they are not committed to the repo or published. Sources, in order: (1) Tobias's own captures of the apps he has installed (Sublime for sure; Zed/VS Code are free and capturable on a private Xvfb or his desktop) on the same fixture file and same scene list, which also makes them comparable; (2) official marketing screenshots and press kits (Linear, Zed, iA Writer, Ghostty docs) fetched with WebFetch and stored under a gitignored refs/ directory with a SOURCES.md of URLs and fetch dates; (3) no scraping of paywalled or licensed galleries. Marketing shots are staged, so the council is told they are aspirational, not like-for-like; captured Sublime is the calibration anchor. Nothing here imitates or republishes a third party's brand.
findings.evidence: Best-design research report (Linear, Zed, VS Code, Sublime, Ghostty, iA Writer); Law 1 amendment 2026-10-26 allows Sublime drives as a test tool

findings.title: Council: members, blindness, rubric
findings.detail: Members: Codex gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh (CLAUDE.md Law 10: Opus-grade, `codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -i <png>... -o out.md`) and Claude Opus. Two members only: tstack council expects three providers and reports an unreachable one rather than substituting, so we name members explicitly. No Fable (Law 10). Sonnet is not a member; Sonnet only runs scripts. Rubric: the 10 criteria from the best-design research (C1 type rendering, C2 contrast hierarchy, C3 colour discipline, C4 chrome quietness, C5 tab bar, C6 status and gutter, C7 minimap and scrollbar, C8 find and palette, C9 selection/caret/match states, C10 empty and edge states), anchors 1/3/5, checked into docs/design/rubric.md. Motion is excluded from screenshot grading (graded from code). Blind pass: the member sees two images per scene labelled X and Y in random order, with no word on which is new, and returns per criterion a score for each plus a one-sentence evidence quote tied to a pixel region. Controls: one scene pair is submitted with identical images (expect equal scores; disagreement measures noise) and the captured Sublime scene is scored as calibration. Sighted pass: after blind scoring, members are told which is the candidate and asked for the top 3 concrete fixes ranked, each naming the token or layout element.
findings.evidence: tstack skills/council/SKILL.md and sol-loop/SKILL.md (per research input); codex exec --help shows -i/--image and --output-schema

findings.title: Disagreement and acceptance
findings.detail: Per criterion, score = mean of the two members; a disagreement of 2 or more points on a criterion is not averaged away, it is listed with both quotes and Tobias or the coordinator decides (the tstack rule: orchestrator judgment, no vote). Council acceptance: candidate median over scenes is not lower on any criterion beyond the measured noise (identical-pair control gap) and higher on at least one the change targets. Then Tobias's eye on a before/after contact sheet is the second, binding half (Law 1: milestones exit by use; scores advisory). Cost gate per Law 4: each candidate bead states memory and typing-path cost with derivation as the workups README does (for example 01 is 0 B because the same 29 tokens change value; 02 net -971,200 B is derived there); any candidate that adds allocation on input -> mutation -> layout -> submit is rejected by Law 2 and the counting-allocator test regardless of score. The only enforced perf guard stays G1 in tests/editor_test.c; benches are notes only.

findings.title: Proposing a change: mock first, then a one-worker bead
findings.detail: Step 1 mock: the sighted pass or Tobias names a weakness; a worker produces an SVG/PNG mock (as the workups did, cairo drawn at the capture resolution) and the council grades the mock against the baseline blind, cheaply, before any code. Step 2 bead: only mocks that win the council and Tobias's eye become a one-worker bead with scope, acceptance (red test first: for token changes a contrast-ratio test on theme values, for layout changes a render/layout test), files, and the cost derivation. Step 3: the harness re-captures the real build and the same blind comparison runs on real pixels, since mocks lie about glyph rendering and grid snapping (every chrome bar is a whole number of rows, per the workups README grid fact). One axis changes per candidate so score deltas are attributable; hill-climb = one accepted candidate becomes the new baseline.
findings.evidence: docs/design/workups-2026-10-21/README.md (grid fact; mocks were SVG+PNG); CLAUDE.md Law 9

findings.title: Stopping rule
findings.detail: Per candidate: max 3 council rounds (copied from sol-loop default; no extension, there is no security/data-loss class here), stop earlier if a round yields only nits (no criterion delta beyond the control noise). Per campaign: stop when Tobias says the look is done by use, or when two consecutive accepted-candidate attempts fail to raise any criterion beyond noise (plateau). Never stop on a numeric total alone, since ten 1-5 scores are a coarse proxy. The campaign is explicitly not for today; the order of work is bug fixes first (the minimap and find bugs from the other topics), because an empty-tab minimap artefact is C10=1 regardless of palette.
findings.evidence: tstack sol-loop (3 rounds, nit-only stop); research root cause: edit-b0j still open since 2026-10-10

findings.title: Quota and lanes
findings.detail: Calls per iteration, derived from the design above (P, arithmetic, not measured usage): blind pass = 2 members x 2 themes with one batched call each carrying that theme's 6 scene pairs = 4 calls; control and calibration ride inside those same calls (extra images, no extra calls); sighted fix pass = 2 calls (one per member, dark+light together) = 6 calls per candidate round. Fallback if batching blurs detail: one call per scene per member = 2x12 = 24 calls per blind pass. Three rounds per candidate = 18 calls (P: 6x3) in the batched design. Lanes: Codex sol xhigh is the preferred worker while Codex is behind pace (Law 10, PLAN 5.7); Opus member is one call per batch from the main coordinator session (Opus is permitted to coordinate); capture and scoring scripts are Sonnet/Haiku beads or Codex; implementation beads follow existing routing. Before each dispatch wave the coordinator runs `quota` and defers Claude calls if any window is more than +2 % ahead of pace (Law 11); Codex calls shift to the other lane when it is the one ahead. No number of campaigns is committed here; the real cost per call is to be measured on the first run and written into the worklog.

findings.title: What is not in the protocol on purpose
findings.detail: No automatic merge on score. No Gemini substitute. No screenshots of real files from Tobias's profile (fixtures only, so nothing private reaches a model). No redistributing third-party images. No taste judgments about brand identity (name 'sublimité', icon) in the rubric; those stay Tobias's.

root_causes: There is no gradeable standard: edit-b0j (visual spec, open since 2026-10-10) never produced a scored rubric, and the five 2026-10-21 workups exist as pictures only, with no repeatable capture or scoring.
Screenshots of the installed build were taken ad hoc on a hand-started Xvfb (workups baseline), so before/after comparisons are not reproducible.
tstack council is a code-review loop with no design rubric, so the design hill-climb needs its own rubric, rendering and blind A/B logic.

proposed_beads.title: Scene-capture harness: tools/design_shots.sh renders 6 scenes x 2 themes deterministically
proposed_beads.scope: Script that starts a private Xvfb (3296x2060x24, pinned DPI, -noreset), private XDG dirs, EDIT_REFUSE_REAL_DISPLAY=1, uses tools/with_display_lock.sh, opens frozen fixtures from tests/fixtures/design/ (C file, mkcorpus large file with fixed seed and size, many-tab set), drives scenes with xdotool (empty tab, code, find with matches, palette, many tabs, large file with minimap) for dark and light, waits for stable frames, writes PNGs plus manifest.json (scene, theme, sha256, DPI, binary hash, power state from /sys/class/power_supply/BAT0/status). No editor changes.
proposed_beads.acceptance: Red first: tests/design_shots_test.sh expects manifest.json to list 12 entries and each PNG to exist and have more than one colour; fails because the script does not exist. Green after. Second test runs the harness twice and byte-compares PNGs, listing differing scenes (blinking caret must be handled so static scenes match). Kills its Xvfb and editor on exit, even on failure. Every number in the script (window size, wait frames) has a derivation comment.

proposed_beads.title: Design rubric and reference-sheet spec
proposed_beads.scope: Check the 10 criteria with 1/3/5 anchors into docs/design/rubric.md (WCAG ratios derived as in the workups README), docs/design/references.md with the exemplar list (pending Tobias's pick), legal sourcing rules and a SOURCES template, and a .gitignore entry for docs/design/refs/. No code.
proposed_beads.acceptance: A lint script tests/rubric_lint_test.py (red first: file missing) checks that all 10 criteria exist with 1, 3 and 5 anchors and that any numeric anchor has a derivation or tag (P/M/E/G). Tobias approves the exemplar list before any council run.

proposed_beads.title: Council runner: blind pairwise scoring with Codex sol and Opus, JSON output and aggregation
proposed_beads.scope: tools/council_run.py sends, per theme, the scene pairs (baseline vs candidate in random seeded order, one identical control pair, optionally the Sublime calibration image) plus the rubric to codex exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh -s read-only --skip-git-repo-check -i <png...> --output-schema <schema.json> -o out.json (< /dev/null for background use), and to an Opus run through the claude CLI with the same prompt; aggregate script computes per-criterion mean, member disagreement of 2 or more, control-pair noise, regression list, and writes docs/reviews/design-council-<date>.md. Dry-run mode prints calls and the count without invoking models. Scores marked advisory.
proposed_beads.acceptance: Red first: tests/council_aggregate_test.py feeds two canned JSON score files and expects mean, disagreement list, noise gap and regression list; fails before the script exists. Schema rejects a score outside 1-5 or a missing criterion; the dry-run count equals 4 calls for the batched design (2 members x 2 themes), asserted in the test. The blind prompt must not contain the words baseline, candidate, new or old (test greps the generated prompt).
